la-forme-rytirska-praha.seoTitulek: La Forme Prague Old Town – bakery café & breakfast
la-forme-rytirska-praha.seoPopis: La Forme on Rytířská, steps from Old Town Square: one of Prague's best-rated bakeries with filled croissants, danishes and specialty coffee. Open from 7:30.
la-forme-rytirska-praha.popis:
La Forme is one of Prague's best-rated bakeries, and in August 2026 it opened its third and largest location right in the historic centre – on Rytířská street, a short walk from Můstek and Old Town Square. Unlike the tiny original bakery in Dejvice, here you can sit down: the café has around twenty seats and the pastries are baked on site.

Croissants, danishes and Scandinavian style

Everything is baked right here: filled croissants, playful danishes and sweet swirls, served with specialty coffee or matcha. The interior is bright and minimalist, inspired by Scandinavia.

Breakfast in the city centre

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and at 8:00 at weekends, which makes it one of the few good options for an early breakfast in the Old Town before the crowds arrive.
la-forme-rytirska-praha.tip: Come in the morning – pastries at La Forme often sell out early. Pick a filled croissant or a danish and pair it with a flat white or matcha.

stranou-praha.seoTitulek: Stranou Prague Malá Strana – breakfast & brunch
stranou-praha.seoPopis: Stranou in Malá Strana, near Petřín funicular: cosy bistro with breakfast from 7:30, plum pancakes, creamy scrambled eggs and sourdough from Tisse Bakery.
stranou-praha.popis:
Stranou is a small bistro with a big heart on Hellichova street in Malá Strana (Lesser Town), a few minutes from Újezd and the Petřín funicular – and about ten minutes' walk from Charles Bridge. In the morning it smells of freshly baked cake and specialty coffee, and the vaulted interior is bright and cosy.

Breakfast and brunch from early morning

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and 8:30 at weekends. The breakfast menu is served from 8:00 to 15:00 and changes with the seasons – think a bistro plate with ham off the bone or a sausage from a family butcher, fried egg, Czech hermelín cheese and sourdough from Tisse Bakery, creamy scrambled eggs with pumpkin crunch, a vegan and gluten-free savoury oat porridge or plum pancakes with quark cream and gingerbread crumble.

Lunch menu

From 11:00 to 15:00 there is also a lunch menu – soup of the day, Swedish meatballs, quesadilla or a vegan kimchi poke bowl. Gluten-free bread is available.
stranou-praha.tip: Order the creamy scrambled eggs with pumpkin crunch, or the plum pancakes with gingerbread crumble if you have a sweet tooth. A perfect stop before or after walking up Petřín Hill.

coffee-bird-praha.seoTitulek: Coffee Bird Prague – breakfast & brunch near Národní
coffee-bird-praha.seoPopis: Coffee Bird on Pštrossova, near the National Theatre: a cosy living-room style café with eggs, homemade granola, semolina porridge and French toast. Open daily.
coffee-bird-praha.popis:
Coffee Bird is a small breakfast café on Pštrossova street, right next to the well-known Globe bookstore and a short walk from the National Theatre and the Vltava riverbank. It was opened in summer 2026 by a young couple, Adéla and Bruno Kraus, and at weekends there is often a queue.

Breakfast and brunch until 14:00

The menu was created by Adéla, who previously cooked at some of Prague's favourite brunch spots, Etapa and Sestava. Expect egg dishes, homemade granola, Czech semolina porridge with chocolate and French toast with blueberry compote. Coffee comes from Doubleshot roastery, bread from Zrno Zrnko bakery, and cakes and cookies are baked on site.

Like breakfast at a friend's place

The space seats around twenty and feels like a living room: a big wooden table, retro furniture, a bookshelf and a chest of drawers with yellow drawers. There is no classic bar – staff move freely between the guests.
coffee-bird-praha.tip: Breakfast is served until 14:00. Try the semolina porridge with chocolate – a Czech childhood classic – or the French toast with blueberry compote.

kavarna-muna-praha.seoTitulek: Muna Prague – Argentine medialunas & specialty coffee
kavarna-muna-praha.seoPopis: Kavárna Muna on Myslíkova, New Town: Argentine medialunas – softer, sweeter cousins of the croissant – with specialty coffee. Open daily from 8:00.
kavarna-muna-praha.popis:
Muna on Myslíkova street brings a piece of Argentina to the centre of Prague. If you're looking for a slow morning coffee, a sweet breakfast or an afternoon break with exceptional pastries, Muna is one of the most interesting newcomers on the Prague food scene.

Argentina's answer to the croissant

The star here are medialunas – traditional Argentine pastries that look like croissants but are softer, more tender and slightly sweet. In Argentina they are part of everyday life, usually eaten with coffee at breakfast or in the afternoon. You'll find classic medialunas as well as almond or pistachio filled versions and regular seasonal specials.

Specialty coffee and a relaxed vibe

Coffee comes from Father's Coffee Roastery. In the morning it's a breakfast spot, during the day a coffee stop, and in the evening the big central table fills with Spanish wine and cava. Open every day from 8:00, with outdoor seating and dogs welcome.
kavarna-muna-praha.tip: Try a classic medialuna first, then a pistachio one. They are softer and sweeter than a French croissant – perfect with a flat white.
